title: mlflow-skinny/mlflow-tracing on Windows: clone with core.symlinks enabled or turn on Developer Mode before building from source
answers: How do I build mlflow-skinny from source on Windows without the 'not a directory' error?
Building mlflow-tracing wheel on Windows produces a package with no modules, what do I change?
What git flag is needed to clone mlflow so libs/skinny/mlflow becomes a real directory on Windows?
body:
Path: libs/skinny/setup.py and libs/tracing/setup.py are the build-time entry points that check whether the libs/<pkg>/mlflow symlink resolved; their error message names the fix.
Rule: on Windows, the linked package only materializes if git creates symlinks at checkout. Either enable Developer Mode (or run elevated), or clone with `git -c core.symlinks=true clone https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow`, then build libs/skinny or libs/tracing from that checkout.
Constraints: the PR's manual test used a fresh `--depth=1` clone; re-cloning with the flag is the path the guard suggests, and Linux and macOS checkouts already resolve the symlinks, so the flag is only needed on Windows.
applies: Source builds of mlflow-skinny or mlflow-tracing on Windows; irrelevant on Linux/macOS or when installing published wheels from PyPI.
says: Building the lightweight client from source on Windows fails with a directory error.
Creating the tracing package on Windows produces an empty archive with no modules.
Need the source installation for the minimal client to work properly on Windows.
Package built from source on Windows is missing its internal module folders.
search: Building mlflow-skinny or mlflow-tracing from source on Windows requires enabling Developer Mode or cloning with git -c core.symlinks=true so the package symlink resolves. Build entry points libs/skinny/setup.py and libs/tracing/setup.py verify that libs/<pkg>/mlflow exists as a directory and report the error. The rule applies only to Windows source builds and is irrelevant on Linux, macOS, or when installing prebuilt wheels from PyPI.
